scope: Recover the correct Flash-Next MoESQ lane, reject performance-neutral full-BF16 expert streaming, convert paired-sparse NVFP4 experts to Strata W4A8, and exercise the complete pack on B550.

bf16_streaming_decision.verdict: Full BF16 routed-expert streaming can be byte-exact but is not performance-neutral on B550: broad prompt unions approach the full 225 GiB expert set, exceed RAM, and are storage-bound. This does not apply to the small dense/shared or PLE-row working sets.
bf16_streaming_decision.evidence_basis: Exact geometry and routing union from the Flash-Next planner plus the resumed B550 direct storage and exact-shape BF16 compute measurements; the raw resumed-session logs were not retained, so this receipt records the decision and the MoESQ pack below is the durable executable lane.

reconstructed_shard.name: model-00003-of-00049.safetensors
reconstructed_shard.method: verified head and tail ranges plus unchanged BF16 PLE tensors, copied in safetensors offset order

converter.focused_tests: uv run --python 3.12 --with numpy python -m unittest tools.test_moesq_pack: 6/6 OK on Mac and B550
converter.output_layout: 48 layers x 512 experts; ggml type 40 gate/up/down; 2,764,816 bytes per expert

weight_contract.activation_contract: Strata W4A8 Q8_1; MoESQ input_global_scale is not applied

correctness_incident_and_fix.initial_error: Writing weight_global_scale directly as a Strata multiplier made the real grouped expert output 100.000% off.
correctness_incident_and_fix.cause: MoESQ source divides by weight_global_scale; Strata tails multiply.
correctness_incident_and_fix.post_fix_real_expert_error: 1.100% on layer 0 expert 0, from two Q8_1 activation roundings

converter.naive_rtn_control: tools/qwen4exp_quant_aware_rco.py now has --assignment-mode all-width --all-width-bits 4; its six host-safe tests pass. This is a correctness-first fixed group-32 RTN measurement control, not a packed artifact.

engine_smoke.command_family: clean-main SM86 strata, physical GPU1, native IQ2_XS dense/base, MoESQ NVFP4 experts, direct PLE, INT8 KV, prefill 512, spec 2, greedy eight tokens
engine_smoke.cache_path_observation: The two auto-cache runs used different GPU/CPU expert placements and produced different token IDs. This is an engine cache-path reproducibility boundary, not a converter parity failure.
engine_smoke.no_cache_boundary: The native engine contract requires --spec >=2, while --spec needs the expert residency table. --expert-cache 0 completed the two-token CPU prefill but exited 2 before decode; --spec 1 was refused at startup. No no-cache decode claim is made.

non_claims: This is a hybrid research pack: MoESQ routed experts are converted, while dense/index/tokenizer/PLE come from the existing calibrated IQ2_XS base. It is not byte-equivalent to a whole MoESQ checkpoint.
Strata executes the experts as generic W4A8 Q8_1 on SM86, not native Blackwell paired-sparse W4A4; no MoESQ-equivalent W4A4 quality claim is made.
The reciprocal global multiplier is rounded once to F32, so effective weights are not bit-exact despite exact FP4 codes and E4M3 bytes.
No perplexity, KL, held-out quality, coding evaluation, serving deployment, router integration, publication, or Hugging Face upload was run.
The two short throughput observations are cold-load one-shots with different PLE devices, not matched medians or a same-day control against another model.
Different auto-cache token IDs are recorded as a boundary; no deterministic full-model output claim is made.
The failed no-cache arms are not accepted as engine smokes; they only establish the current native-pack/spec residency-table contract.
